The nitrogen is single-bonded to a tert-butyl group on the left, and it is connected on the right to a nitrilium-like carbon fragment represented as a triple bond extending to a terminal methyl group. Curved arrows are present, but the question says to ignore the arrows. Reasoning: Ignoring the arrows, the molecular graph is methyl carbon bonded to a carbon triple-bonded to positively charged nitrogen, written as CC#[N+]. planner_metadata.image_role: Read the central N with a positive charge, its single bond to a tert-butyl carbon on the left bearing three methyl groups, and its triple-bonded connection to a carbon chain on the right that terminates in a methyl group; ignore the curved reaction arrows around the N/triple-bond region.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction to produce a SMILES expression for the pictured transition-state structure and to ignore all arrows rather than treating them as bonds.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES rules: aliphatic carbons are written as C, a positively charged nitrogen must be bracketed as [N+], triple bonds are denoted by #, and branches from a tetrahedral carbon are written in parentheses. Encode tert-butyl as C(C)(C)C attached to [N+], and the methyl–carbon-triple-nitrogen fragment as CC#[N+].
